- A runnable test plan (burst vs steady-state) we can run during our allowed windows.
- Clear guidance on client-side rate limits to avoid queueing/timeouts.

Joe

Joe — thanks, good to be moving. Attached is our proposed MAP + perf evaluation plan (redwood_map_perf_plan.pdf). High-level summary below; please review and confirm sign-off by EOD 2026-05-04 so we can reserve a dedicated pool for the test window.

MAP highlights (milestones and owners):
- 5/05: Test environment & config confirmed (Redwood: dylan; Acme: Joe)
- 5/06–5/08: Baseline steady-state run (4h windows) — measure p50/p95 latency, TTFT, throughput
- 5/09: Controlled burst windows (10 x 1-min bursts + 1 x 15-min sustained spike) — observe queueing/backpressure
- 5/10: Results summary and go/no-go for procurement

Evaluation metrics (primary):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) median and p95
- Per-request throughput (tokens/sec), end-to-end request latency (p50/p95)
- Concurrency behavior: queued requests, 429/503 counts, retry amplification risk

Test matrix (attached):
- Models: redwood-1.3b-q4_1, redwood-7b-8k (quantized variant)
- Concurrency points: 50, 200, 500, 1000 concurrent request levels
- Payload sizes: short (50 tokens), medium (150 tokens), long (800 tokens)

Rate-limit guidance (initial):
- Client-side token bucket recommended: burst capacity = 3x steady rate, refill rate = steady RPS target
- For bursts we suggest smoothing over 10s windows to avoid synchronized spikes against the serving pool

Quick note on queueing: Redwood will expose per-route queue depth and admission metrics. For observed spikes where queue depth hits the configured limit, the runtime will either (a) apply backpressure with 429 responses or (b) autoscale/route to a higher-capacity tier depending on policy. We will share the admission-config we plan to use in the config attachment.

Attachments: redwood_map_perf_plan.pdf (contains exact test commands, expected metrics, and dashboards), concurrency_test_config.yaml

Next step: confirm the matrix and owners by 5/04 and we'll schedule the steady-state slot.

—Dylan

Subject: Pilot perf results & recommended rate-limit tuning (baseline + bursts)

Joe / team — summary of the runs we completed in the reserved Dedicated pool; attached raw CSVs in concurrency_results_q1.csv and the updated MAP doc (acme_signed_mop.docx) that includes the acceptance criteria and recommended client knobs.

Quick summary (high level):
- Test environment: Dedicated pool (4x V100-equivalent), redwood-7b-8k (quantized) and redwood-1.3b-q4_1 for small payloads.
- Steady-state (5/06, 4h window): target 200 RPS (medium payload) sustained
  - p50 latency (medium): 68 ms
  - p95 latency (medium): 188 ms
  - median TTFT: 74 ms; p95 TTFT: 95 ms
- Concurrency sweep: 50 / 200 / 500 / 1000 concurrent request levels (mixed payloads)
  - up to 500 concurrent: system remained stable, p95 latency increased linearly (expected), retry amplification minimal
  - at 1000 concurrent bursts (10 x 60s bursts + 15m sustained spike): observed significant queueing and increased 429 responses when admission limit hit. Median TTFT during the immediate peaks spiked to ~160 ms; p95 request latency exceeded 600 ms in the worst windows.

Failure modes observed:
- Synchronized spikes from naive clients cause queue depth to grow quickly and trigger admission control (429). Retries without jitter caused short-term retry storms amplifying load.
- When sustained spike exceeded autoscaling window, end-to-end latency climbed and a small portion (~1.8%) of requests saw 5xx transient errors during scale-up.

Recommended client-side knobs (table in attached MAP; summary):
- Token-bucket refill target: set steady refill ~= 700 RPS for your medium endpoint; burst capacity = 3x (allow short 2–3x bursts)
- Burst smoothing window: 10s sliding window to spread bursts; this reduces synchronized queueing events by ~60% in our sim
- Retry policy: up to 2 retries with exponential backoff starting at 150ms + full jitter; do not retry on 5xx/429 unless backoff applies and cap total client-side concurrency

Server-side options (Redwood):
- We can increase admission threshold for your pool for the pilot (temporarily) to accommodate 1.2k RPS with slightly higher cost and a 30–90s autoscale lag.
- Enable adaptive admission: dynamic drop/route to fallback model variant when queue depth exceeds X to preserve p95 latency for gold-tier routes.

Attached: concurrency_results_q1.csv (raw), acme_signed_mop.docx (MAP with acceptance criteria), redwood_map_perf_plan.pdf (original plan).

Next steps:
- We will send an updated MAP with the recommended client knobs embedded and a short 15-minute handoff on 5/13 to walk procurement/legal through the throttling behavior and acceptance criteria.
- Action items:
  - Joe: confirm you are comfortable with the token-bucket suggestion and the proposed retry limits by EOD 5/11
  - Lauren/Marissa: we'll prepare a 1-page appendix for the SOW describing the admission model and fallback behavior.

If you want, we can also run an additional targeted burst with your exact client retry behavior to show expected failure modes before signature.

—Dylan
